The saved raw files contain 592 RTO and 586 WFH records. The cleaning script combines RTO first, so a URI appearing in both searches retains the RTO label. The resulting saved dataset contains 1,137 posts (577 RTO, 560 WFH).

Saved RTO post timestamps span 25 August to 29 September 2026; WFH timestamps span 15 to 29 September 2026 (UTC, ignoring missing timestamps). These are observed post-date ranges, not guaranteed collection windows. The different time coverage and latest-result selection limit direct population comparisons. This analysis reads the frozen files and does not collect fresh data.

For the text and clustering sections, we retain only posts with at least one language tag and with **every tag equal to `en` or an English regional variant** (case-insensitive). This leaves 751 English-labelled posts. We exclude 345 records without language tags and 41 with non-English or mixed tags. This is a metadata-based rule, not independent language verification; some excluded unlabelled posts may be English, and tagged posts may be mislabelled.

URLs, including bare domains and query strings, and account mentions are removed. Text is tokenised into lowercase words; English stop words, tokens containing non-ASCII letters or nonletters, and one-letter tokens are removed. Twenty-four English-labelled posts have no retained tokens, leaving **727 usable posts: 371 RTO and 356 WFH**. Full word forms are retained for readable descriptive charts. The per-post audit is saved in `outputs/text/inclusion_audit.csv`.

```{r text-inclusion-table, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(read.csv("outputs/text/sample_counts.csv"),
             caption = "Text-analysis inclusion decisions by search group")
```

The earlier 20-post review identified political-office references, a Swedish post and link-only material. It was a diagnostic sample, not a complete relevance screen. No topic-based exclusions or text-based deduplication are applied here: distinct URIs can repeat the same message. Results therefore describe **English-labelled search results**, not a verified corpus of workplace-only discussion. The network section uses its own separately collected thread sample; these text-analysis filters do not alter it.
